lines.japanese: 「あ、もしもし？　お忙しいところ畏れいります。わたくし千歳と申しますが、軽部店長はいらっ……あ、マスターすか？」
lines.english: “Hello? Sorry to trouble you. This is Chitose. May I speak to the manager, Mr. Karube—oh, boss, is that you?”

lines.japanese: 「……こほん」
lines.english: “...Ahem.”

lines.japanese: 「こんばんは！　千歳鷲介、さすらいの自由人！　アレキサンダーでバイトするため、白馬に乗ってやってきました！」
lines.english: “Good evening! Shusuke Chitose, wandering free spirit! I’ve come riding in on a white horse to work at Alexander!”

lines.japanese: 「好きな古代都市はアレキサンドリア、好きな健康器具はエキスパンダー！　短いあいだですがお世話になります、以後ヨロシク！　イェー！　愛を取りもどせイェー！」
lines.english: “My favorite ancient city is Alexandria! My favorite piece of exercise equipment is a chest expander! I'll only be with you a short while, but I'm glad to be aboard! Yeah! Take Back the Love! Yeah!”

lines.japanese: ──なんちって！！（必死）
lines.english: —Just kidding!! (Desperate.)
“...Phew.”

lines.japanese: と、まあ、そんな感じで。
lines.english: And, well, that's about how it went.

lines.japanese: その後、ちゃんと真面目な話もしたりして通話終了。
lines.english: We had a proper, serious conversation afterward, and then the call ended.

lines.japanese: こうして俺は、めでたくアレキサンダー花水木通り店でアルバイトをさせていただくことになりました。
lines.english: And so I was officially granted the privilege of working part-time at Alexander's Hanamizuki Avenue branch.

lines.japanese: 「あー緊張した」
lines.english: “God, that was nerve-racking.”

lines.japanese: マスターはさっそく今日からでもいいと仰ってくださったのですが、とりあえず俺にも米田さんから戴いた仕事があるので、初出勤はあす２８日とさせていただきました。
lines.english: The boss generously said I could start as soon as today, but I had work from Yoneda to finish first, so we settled on tomorrow, the twenty-eighth, for my inaugural shift.

lines.japanese: てなわけで、まあ、新しい職場への不安やら緊張やらもあるんですが、差しあたっては在宅仕事からやっつけてしまわねばなりません。
lines.english: Naturally, I felt some anxiety and tension about starting at a new workplace, but first I had to knock out the work waiting for me at home.

lines.japanese: さいわい今日はこのあとの≪約束≫もないので、俺には夜まで時間がたっぷりあります。
lines.english: Fortunately, I had no other ≪engagements≫ today, which left me plenty of time before nightfall.

lines.japanese: ようし、始めよう。
lines.english: All right. Let’s begin.

lines.japanese: 「ッシャァァァ！」
lines.english: “HRRAAAAAH!”

lines.japanese: 気合を入れて立ちあがると、箱買いしてある栄養ドリンクをポータブル冷蔵庫から一本取りだし、腰に手を当てキュッと一気におじさん飲み。
lines.english: I sprang to my feet, fired up, pulled one of the energy drinks I bought by the case from my portable fridge, planted a hand on my hip, and downed it in one brisk old-man gulp.

lines.japanese: そんな俺を必要以上に明るい笑顔で見守っているのは、隅が黄ばみかけた古いポスター。
lines.english: Watching over me with an unnecessarily radiant smile was an old poster whose corners had begun to yellow.

lines.japanese: 「こんばんは！」
lines.english: “Good evening!”

lines.japanese: 俺は四辺形の中の若々しい彼らにも負けない笑顔で、サムズアップを返しました。
lines.english: I flashed the youthful figures inside the rectangle a smile every bit as bright and gave them a thumbs-up.

lines.japanese: なぜ夜でもないのに「こんばんは」なのかと申しますと、それがフリッキー５のヨッくんこと足利美樹氏の口癖だったからです。
lines.english: Why 'good evening' when it wasn't even night? Because it was the catchphrase of Yoshiki Ashikaga—Yoshi of the Fricky Five.

lines.japanese: 十代の瑞々しさあふれる少年たち（もちろんリアルの彼らは現在いい歳をしたオトナなんですが）の笑顔に張りあうと、こちらまで否が応にも活力がみなぎろうってもんです。
lines.english: Matching smiles with those boys in all the freshness of youth—though naturally, the real men were well into adulthood by now—was enough to fill a fellow with energy whether he liked it or not.

lines.japanese: アゲてこう、アゲてこう。
lines.english: Let's get fired up. Let's get fired up.

lines.japanese: 俺はデスクチェアーに飛びのって原稿用紙を広げました。
lines.english: I sprang into my desk chair and spread out my manuscript paper.

lines.japanese: その横には課題図書、多摩いづみ著『青春はそれを我慢できない』。
lines.english: Beside it lay my assigned reading: Izumi Tama’s *Youth Can’t Resist It*.

lines.japanese: ペン立てからシャープペンシルを掴むと、いい感じのテンションで手と思考が働きはじめるのでした。
lines.english: I grabbed a mechanical pencil from the holder, and once I hit the right groove, my hand and brain got moving.

lines.japanese: いや、だって、ねえ？
lines.english: I mean, come on. You know?

lines.japanese: 馬鹿っぽいノリで一丁、なんて米田さんは簡単に言うけど、そんな、言うほど簡単には行かないんすよ？　ほら、俺って根っこの部分は真面目だし？
lines.english: Yoneda made it sound so easy: 'Give me something nice and stupid.' But it wasn't that simple, you know? I mean, deep down, I'm a serious guy, right?

lines.japanese: なんつってね。
lines.english: Just kidding.

lines.japanese: 「──はい、米田です」
lines.english: “—Hello, Yoneda speaking.”

lines.japanese: 「あ、お世話になってます、アルバイトの千歳です」
lines.english: “Hello. This is Chitose—the part-timer.”

lines.japanese: 「あー、千歳君！　ちょっと、この前、大丈夫だった？」
lines.english: “Oh, Chitose! Hey, were you all right the other day?”

lines.japanese: 「は……この前？　なんでしたっけ？」
lines.english: “Huh...? The other day? What happened?”

lines.japanese: 「ほら、おとといの夜。柳木原の改札んとこで」
lines.english: “You know, the night before last. At the ticket gates in Yanagihara.”

lines.japanese: 「彼女……じゃないんだっけ？　あの女の子が来てから、千歳君いきなり顔色変えちゃって」
lines.english: “That girl—wasn’t she your girlfriend? The moment she showed up, all the color drained out of your face.”

lines.japanese: 「やー、はは……そのことは、あえて思いださないようにしてたんすけど……」
lines.english: Yeah, haha... I'd been trying pretty hard not to remember that...

lines.japanese: 「逃避？」
lines.english: “Avoidance?”

lines.japanese: 「ええ、まさに。正直、あのあと自分がどうやって帰ったかもよく覚えてないっす」
lines.english: “Precisely. Honestly, I barely remember how I got home afterward.”

lines.japanese: 「何事かと思ったよ、彼女置いてさっさと逃げちゃうし。なに、ケンカでもしたの？」
lines.english: “I wondered what had happened. You just abandoned your girlfriend and ran off. Did you two have a fight?”

lines.japanese: 「いやあ、ですから、もとよりケンカという言葉が成立するほどの仲じゃないですしボクら。ま、大したことじゃないっすよ、ええ」
lines.english: No, like I said, we were never close enough to call it a fight in the first place. It's no big deal, really.

lines.japanese: 「とか言いつつ声沈んでるよ？」
lines.english: “You say that, but your voice has gone all gloomy.”

lines.japanese: 「えー？　あ、ほーんとだ。ちょっと待ってください？」
lines.english: Huh? Oh, wow, you're right. Hold on a sec.

lines.japanese: 通話口を離して深呼吸、それからポスターに向かって喝の入れなおし。
lines.english: I moved the phone away, took a deep breath, then turned to the poster to give myself another kick in the pants.

lines.japanese: 「こんばんは！」
lines.english: “Good evening!”

lines.japanese: おし、オーケイ。
lines.english: There. Good to go.

lines.japanese: 「もしもし！　お待たせしました千歳です！　納豆に付いてくる醤油をこぼさず開けるのが得意です、こんばんは！」
lines.english: “Hello! Sorry to keep you waiting; Chitose speaking! My special talent is opening the little soy-sauce packet that comes with fermented soybeans without spilling it! Good evening!”

lines.japanese: 「あーら、おなかから声出しちゃってー。おねえさん、元気な男の子は大好きよー」
lines.english: “My, you're projecting all the way from your diaphragm. I do love an energetic young man.”

lines.japanese: 「いやっほう！　好きの二文字でみなぎるパワー！」
lines.english: “Woo-hoo! One little ‘like’ and I'm bursting with power!”

lines.japanese: 「いやあ、女のひとってホント偉大ですよね。言葉ひとつで男のテンションを上げ下げしちゃうわけじゃないすか。ある意味怖いっすよね、ある意味そこらじゅうクレオパトラっすよね」
lines.english: Man, women are amazing, aren't they? One word and they can send a guy's energy straight up or straight down. Kinda scary, in a way. It's like Cleopatras everywhere you look.

lines.japanese: 「ええー？　そんなのべつに、女に限った話じゃないでしょー？　だってさ、誰であれ人間の発する意思表示には、言葉どころか目線ひとつ取ったって相手の感情を揺さぶっちゃう力が──」
lines.english: “Really? That hardly applies only to women. Any sign of what another person thinks—even a glance, never mind words—has the power to stir somebody else's emotions—”

lines.japanese: 「──やめた。ごめんね、おとなって知ってることが多いぶん語りだすと長いんだ。言葉で伝えるのが不可能なことを言葉で伝えようとしたって、ただ説教くさくなるだけなのにね。えっと、これ何の電話？」
lines.english: “—Never mind. Sorry. Adults know so much that once we start talking, we go on forever. Trying to convey in words what words can't convey only makes you sound preachy. Um, what was this call about?”

lines.japanese: 「ああ、はい、『青春はそれを我慢できない』の紹介文が大体あがりそうなんで、その報告っす」
lines.english: “Right. I’m nearly finished with the blurb for *Youth Can’t Resist It*, so I wanted to let you know.”

lines.japanese: 「おー、早いねー。助かるねー。フットワークのいいライターは編集者に重宝されるよー」
lines.english: “Oh, that was fast. What a help. Editors treasure writers who turn things around quickly.”

lines.japanese: 「はい、重宝されたくて千歳鷲介がんばりました！　米田さんに生殺与奪を握られています、こんばんは！」
lines.english: Yes! Shusuke Chitose worked his butt off because he wants to be useful! Yoneda holds the power of life and death over me! Good evening!

lines.japanese: 「ああ……そういうことね。たしか、書籍紹介をもうひと枠欲しいんだったよね？」
lines.english: “Ah... I see now. You wanted another slot in the book column, didn’t you?”

lines.japanese: 「はい！　なんとか工面していただけると！」
lines.english: “Yes! If there’s any way you could make it work!”

lines.japanese: 「いいよ」
lines.english: “Sure.”

lines.japanese: 「いや、そんなご無体なことおっしゃらず！」
lines.english: “No, please—don't be so cruel!”

lines.japanese: 「だから、いいってば」
lines.english: “I said sure.”

lines.japanese: 「分かります！　分かりますけど、そこをなんとか米田さんの力で──」
lines.english: “I understand! Believe me, I do, but if you could somehow use your influence to—”

lines.japanese: 「──て、えええ、いんすか！？」
lines.english: “—Wait, what? You mean yes?!”

lines.japanese: 「なに、反対してほしいの？」
lines.english: “What, did you want me to object?”

lines.japanese: 「まさか！　や、でも米田さん、この前お願いしたときはあんまり好感触じゃなかったから」
lines.english: “Of course not! But when I asked the other day, you didn’t sound very encouraging.”

lines.japanese: 「そりゃあね。こっちはビジネス、給料もらってやってることだもん、私情で軽はずみな返事はできないよ。でもほら、なんて言ったっけ、その子の名前。ていうか本名」
lines.english: “Naturally. This is business. I’m being paid to do it, so I can’t make careless promises for personal reasons. But what was that girl’s name again? Her real name, I mean.”

lines.japanese: 「本名？　はあ、玉泉日和子さんですけど」
lines.english: “Her real name? Hiyoko Tamaizumi.”

lines.japanese: 「そう、それ、ヒヨコちゃん。その名前で下の階に聞いてみたら『細川玉木』のことだって言うじゃない。もー、千歳君もカケルも、最初っからペンネームで言ってよね」
lines.english: “Right, Hiyoko. When I asked the people downstairs about that name, they told me she was Tamaki Hosokawa. Honestly, you and Kakeru should have given me her pen name from the start.”

lines.japanese: 「細川玉木……え、有名なんすか」
lines.english: “Tamaki Hosokawa... Is she famous?”

lines.japanese: 「去年、うちのジュニア向け小説コンテストで銀賞獲った子だよ。デビュー作なんか、何度か重版かかるほど売れてるってば」
lines.english: “She won the silver prize in our young-adult fiction contest last year. Her debut sold well enough to be reprinted several times.”

lines.japanese: 「うゎお！　期待の大型新人！」
lines.english: “W-wow! A major new talent!”

lines.japanese: 「二作目は期待に応えてくれなかったんだけどね」
lines.english: “Her second book didn’t live up to expectations.”

lines.japanese: 「う、うわーお……」
lines.english: “O-oh. Wow...”

lines.japanese: 「ま、詳細は直接会ったとき話そっか。千歳君、次いつ出て来られる？」
lines.english: “We can discuss the details in person. When can you come in next?”

lines.japanese: 「えーと、アレキサンダーの定休日が木曜だから……」
lines.english: “Let’s see. Alexander closes on Thursdays, so...”

lines.japanese: 「ええ？　アレキサンダーの休みが、千歳君になんの関係？」
lines.english: “What? What does Alexander’s closing day have to do with you?”

lines.japanese: 「ああ、俺あそこでバイトすることになったんすよ。ま、バイトっても非常勤のヘルプ要員なんすけど」
lines.english: “Oh, I’m going to start working there. Only as an occasional extra pair of hands, though.”

lines.japanese: 「へー！　入稿済んだら覗きに行ってみようかなあ。なんか面白そう」
lines.english: “Really? Once this issue goes to press, maybe I’ll drop by. It sounds entertaining.”

lines.japanese: 「え、あの、ねえさん？　あの、面白いとかそういうのないですから。俺もビジネスなんで。給料もらってやることなんで。さすがにそこは真面目に努めますよ？」
lines.english: Uh, listen? There's nothing funny about it. This is business for me too. I'm getting paid to do a job. Of course I'm gonna take it seriously, okay?

lines.japanese: 「そんなこと言ったって、やーはは、軽部先輩のしょーもない冗談に振りまわされてる千歳君の姿が目に浮かぶようだわあ」
lines.english: “You can say that, but—ha ha—I can already picture Karube dragging you through one of his hopeless jokes.”

lines.japanese: 「や、やめてくださいよ縁起でもない」
lines.english: “D-don’t jinx me like that.”

lines.japanese: 「えーと、それじゃあ木曜日……しあさっての３０日とか伺ってもよろしいすか？」
lines.english: “In that case, could I come by Thursday—the thirtieth, three days from now?”

lines.japanese: 「木曜日ね。うん、いいよ。夕方ぐらいに来て」
lines.english: “Thursday. Yes, that’s fine. Come around late afternoon.”

lines.japanese: 「かしこまりましたー。そいじゃ、どーも失礼しまーす」
lines.english: “Understood. Well, then, I'll let you go.”

lines.japanese: にこやかな笑顔を固めたまま通話終了ボタンをぴっ。
lines.english: Still holding my cheerful smile perfectly in place, I pressed the end-call button. Beep.

lines.japanese: 電話疲れの溜息を吐きだしながらベッドにごろり。
lines.english: I let out a sigh, exhausted by all that phoning, and flopped onto the bed.

lines.japanese: 掛け布団の上に転がって天井を見上げながらぽつり。
lines.english: I lay atop the comforter, gazed at the ceiling, and murmured to myself.

lines.japanese: 「……充実してるじゃん。勤労青年、千歳鷲介」
lines.english: “...Look at you, leading such a full life. Shusuke Chitose, industrious young man.”

lines.japanese: 目を閉じて、米田さんがよくやるように、目蓋の上から眼球のマッサージをしてみます。
lines.english: I closed my eyes and tried massaging my eyeballs through the lids, the way Yoneda often did.

lines.japanese: くにくに。
lines.english: Rub, rub.

lines.japanese: あー、こりゃ気持ちいいわあ。
lines.english: Ahh, that felt wonderful.

lines.japanese: くにくに。
lines.english: Rub, rub.

lines.japanese: ……しかし。
lines.english: ...And yet.

lines.japanese: 今更ながら、凄いひとだったんだなあ、日和子さん。
lines.english: Only now was it sinking in just how impressive Hiyoko really was.

lines.japanese: 俺的には、もともと初見がエッセイスト『多摩いづみ』という認識だったから──
lines.english: In my mind, she had started out as the essayist Izumi Tama—

lines.japanese: ──つまり、最初からプー太郎なんかよりぐっとステージの高い世界のお方という認識だったから、いざプロフィールを学生作家とか改められても「なんか凄いひと」という点において大差なかったのですが。
lines.english: —which meant I had always pictured her as someone living in a world far above jobless bums like me. Revising her profile to ‘student novelist’ did nothing to change the basic category: ‘impressive person.’

lines.japanese: そうかあ。部署の違う米田さんでも知ってるぐらい凄いのかあ。
lines.english: So impressive that even Yoneda, in a different department, knew who she was.

lines.japanese: 凄い凄いを連発してる、語彙に乏しい自分が恥ずかしくなるぐらい凄いよなあ。
lines.english: She was so impressive, I was almost embarrassed by the poverty of my vocabulary as I went on calling her impressive. Still, impressive was the word.

lines.japanese: くにくに。
lines.english: Rub, rub.

lines.japanese: 細川玉木、か……。
lines.english: Tamaki Hosokawa, then...

lines.japanese: ふむ。一作目は売れたのに、二作目は『期待に応えられなかった』ってなんでだろう。
lines.english: Hmm. If her first book sold, why had the second “failed to meet expectations”?

lines.japanese: くにくに。
lines.english: Rub, rub.

lines.japanese: 日和子さんの本。細川玉木の本。売れた本と売れなかった本。
lines.english: Hiyoko’s books. Tamaki Hosokawa’s books. The one that sold and the one that did not.

lines.japanese: 気になるな。
lines.english: Now I really wanted to know.

lines.japanese: 「──行くか」
lines.english: “—Let’s go.”

lines.japanese: ぱか、と目を開けて呟きました。
lines.english: My eyes popped open as I said it.

lines.japanese: 俺の「今日」が終わるにはまだ時間があることだし、ねえ、時間があるなら使わないのも勿体ないじゃないですか。
lines.english: There was still time before my 'today' came to an end. And if you had time, letting it go to waste would be... well, a waste, wouldn't it?

lines.japanese: 部屋着のスウェットから軽めの外出着に手早く着替え、財布ひとつ持って部屋を出ました。
lines.english: I quickly changed out of my lounging sweats into light street clothes, took only my wallet, and left the room.

lines.japanese: たしか風見ヶ丘駅前の宮川書店は、２２時までやっていたはず。
lines.english: If memory served, Miyagawa Books outside Kazamigaoka Station stayed open until ten.

lines.japanese: ところで、アレ見えますか？
lines.english: By the way, can you see that?

lines.japanese: ほら、あそこ。天高くそびえる超高層マンション。
lines.english: There, look. That high-rise apartment tower soaring into the heavens.

lines.japanese: あんなもんが駅前に築きあげられてしまったせいで、私ども風見ヶ丘の住民はちょっとどこかへ出かけようってたんびに、ついついアレを見上げてしまうのです。
lines.english: Ever since someone went and erected the thing in front of the station, we residents of Kazamigaoka can't so much as pop out somewhere without finding ourselves looking up at it.

lines.japanese: ──や、失礼。立派な職業のご家庭がお住まいでしょうから、あんなもん呼ばわりしちゃいけませんね。
lines.english: —No, excuse me. People with perfectly respectable jobs must live there, so I really shouldn't call it 'the thing.'

lines.japanese: その誉れ尊きお姿に、さあさあ、かしわ手を打って拝みいりましょう。紅白モチぐらい降ってくるかもしれません。
lines.english: Come, clap your hands in worship before its glorious form. Red-and-white ceremonial rice cakes may even come raining down.

lines.japanese: なんちって、くだらねぇー。
lines.english: Just kidding. What a load of crap.

lines.japanese: 目線を庶民の高さに戻せば、駅の方向から、買い物袋を提げた可愛らしいお嬢さんがひとり歩いてくるではありませんか。
lines.english: When I lowered my gaze to the level of the common people, why, there came a charming young lady walking from the direction of the station, shopping bag in hand.

lines.japanese: 羽田さん家の小鳩さんったら、こんな時間におつかいだなんて、なんていい子なんでしょう。
lines.english: Little Kobato Haneda, out running errands at this hour. What a good girl she was.

lines.japanese: 「こんばんは！」
lines.english: “Good evening!”

lines.japanese: びくっ。
lines.english: Flinch.

lines.japanese: お歌のおにいさんみたいな元気の良い挨拶をしたら、あとずさるほどビックリさせてしまったようです。長ネギのはみ出たポリ袋ががさっと音を立てました。
lines.english: My hearty children's-show-host greeting startled her enough to make her step backward. The plastic bag, with a long green onion poking out of it, gave a loud rustle.

lines.japanese: 「あれぇー？　ちょっと見ないあいだに忘れられちゃったかなあ。えーと、俺、鷲介」
lines.english: “What’s this? Have you forgotten me in the little while we haven’t met? Let’s see, I’m Shusuke.”

lines.japanese: こくっ、こくっ。
lines.english: Nod, nod.

lines.japanese: 「なんだ、分かってるじゃない。よかったあ」
lines.english: “Oh, so you do remember. Thank goodness.”

lines.japanese: 「こ……こんばんはっ」
lines.english: “G-good evening.”

lines.japanese: ぺこり。
lines.english: A little bow.

lines.japanese: 「はーい、こんばんは。小鳩さんはいま帰り？　送ってこっか？」
lines.english: “Hey, evening. Heading home, Kobato? Want me to walk you?”

lines.japanese: ふるふるふる。
lines.english: Shake, shake, shake.

lines.japanese: 「そーお？」
lines.english: “You sure?”

lines.japanese: こくん。
lines.english: Nod.

lines.japanese: 「んー？　子供は遠慮しなくていいんだぞー」
lines.english: “Hmm? Kids don't need to hold back.”

lines.japanese: おっ、考えてる考えてる。
lines.english: Oh, she was thinking. She was thinking.

lines.japanese: だけどやっぱり──
lines.english: But in the end—

lines.japanese: 「だ、だいじょぶです」
lines.english: “I-I’ll be all right.”

lines.japanese: 「そお？　ほんとに？」
lines.english: “Really? Are you sure?”

lines.japanese: こくん。
lines.english: Nod.

lines.japanese: 「あそ？　んじゃあ、気を付けて帰りなさいね。ばいばーい」
lines.english: “All right, then. Be careful on your way home. Bye-bye.”

lines.japanese: 「あ、あのっ」
lines.english: “U-um!”

lines.japanese: 「なにかな？」
lines.english: “What is it?”

lines.japanese: 「ど、どちらへ行かれるんですか」
lines.english: “W-where are you going?”

lines.japanese: 「俺？　ちょっと駅の方まで」
lines.english: “Me? Just down toward the station.”

lines.japanese: 「おし、おしごとですか」
lines.english: “F-for work?”

lines.japanese: 「んー、そうねえ……お仕事に必要なものを買いにいくところ？」
lines.english: “Hmm, I suppose... I’m going to buy something I need for work?”

lines.japanese: 「が、がんばってください」
lines.english: “G-good luck.”

lines.japanese: 「うわあお！　嬉しいこと言ってくれるねえ、小鳩さんは。おにいさん、優しい女の子は大好きよー」
lines.english: “Wow! What a lovely thing to say, Kobato. You certainly know how to make an older guy happy. I've always had a soft spot for sweet girls.”

lines.japanese: ぼっ！
lines.english: Fwoom!

lines.japanese: ははは、赤くなった。
lines.english: Ha ha. She turned red.

lines.japanese: 「い、いってらっしゃい……っ」
lines.english: “T-take care...”

lines.japanese: 「はーい、行ってきまーす」
lines.english: “I will. See you later.”

lines.japanese: ははは、小鳩さんは可愛いなあ。恥ずかしがりぃのくせに一生懸命喋っちゃって。
lines.english: Ha ha, Kobato was adorable. Shy as she was, she was trying so hard to get the words out.

lines.japanese: いやあ、お兄さんに似なくてよかったねえ。
lines.english: Boy, it was a good thing she was nothing like her brother.

lines.japanese: なんつったりして。
lines.english: ...or so I'd say.

lines.japanese: それから俺は、駅前の本屋さんで文庫本を二冊買って帰りました。
lines.english: I went on to the bookstore by the station, bought two paperbacks, and returned home.

lines.japanese: 細川玉木のデビュー作『ほほえみインサイド』は、少女小説コーナーに平置きで積まれていて、俺でも名前ぐらいは耳にしたことがあるその道の大家と堂々肩を並べていました。
lines.english: Tamaki Hosokawa's debut, *Smile Inside*, lay face-out in a stack in the girls' fiction section, proudly shoulder to shoulder with a giant of the genre whose name even I had heard.

lines.japanese: 表紙には、少女漫画っぽい繊細なタッチで、むっとした男女が背中合わせに睨みあっているイラストが描かれていました。
lines.english: The cover bore a delicate illustration in the style of a girls' romance comic: a sulking boy and girl stood back-to-back, glaring.

lines.japanese: 奥付を見ると……第９刷。うわ、すご。
lines.english: I checked the colophon... Ninth printing. Wow.

lines.japanese: もう一冊の『米寿』は、棚の下から二番目の段に、無数の著者名に挟まれて一冊だけ立っていました。
lines.english: Her other book, *Eighty-Eight*, stood alone on the second shelf from the bottom, hemmed in by countless other authors' names.

lines.japanese: 引っこぬいて表紙を確認すると、こちらは一作目と打って変わって、郷愁を感じさせる抽象的な風景画って感じです。
lines.english: I pulled it free and examined the cover. In a complete departure from the first book, this one looked like an abstract, nostalgic landscape.

lines.japanese: たぶん稲穂の揺れる秋の田んぼが描かれているのでしょうけど、あいにく絵画に対する審美眼を養わずに育った身では「なんかよく分かんない」としか表現できません。
lines.english: It was probably meant to depict a field of rice rippling in autumn. Unfortunately, having reached adulthood without cultivating an eye for art, the best I could manage was, 'I dunno. I don't really get it.'

lines.japanese: 奥付を見ると……第２刷。ふむ。
lines.english: I checked the colophon... Second printing. Hmm.

lines.japanese: や、まあ、発行日の差もありますしね。
lines.english: Well, there was a difference in publication dates too.

lines.japanese: 俺はその二冊が入った紙袋を右手に提げ、いろんなことを考えながら夜の道を引きかえしていきました。
lines.english: With the paper bag containing both books hanging from my right hand, I retraced my steps through the night and thought about many things.

lines.japanese: そういやもうすぐ１２月。読書の秋、なんて時季でもなかったですね。
lines.english: Come to think of it, December was almost here. A little late for 'autumn, the season for reading.'

lines.japanese: 明日からアレキサンダーです。がんばりましょう。
lines.english: Tomorrow was my first day at Alexander. Time to give it my best.
